title: Am Brunnen
desc: The water is free and somebody will tell you
setting: A hot afternoon on the square, with a two-franc bottle of water in your hand.

options.feedback: She is going somewhere with this. Answer and let her get there.

options.es: Grüezi. Ja, es ist warm heute.
options.en: Grüezi. Yes, it is warm today.
options.feedback: The weather, offered back. That is how a conversation starts here.
She greeted you first. One word back leaves the greeting hanging.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Sie müssen das Wasser nicht kaufen. Dort ist ein Brunnen.
steps.en: You do not have to buy water. There is a fountain over there.

options.feedback: The obvious question, and asking it is how you stop buying water for good.
She has just saved you two francs a day. Take it.

options.es: Das Wasser im Brunnen? Nein, merci.
options.en: The water in the fountain? No, thanks.
options.feedback: She is not offering you puddle water. Almost every fountain in the country runs drinking water.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Natürlich. Fast alle Brunnen sind Trinkwasser.
steps.en: Of course. Almost all the fountains are drinking water.

options.feedback: Exactly the right follow-up. There is a sign, and it says kein Trinkwasser.
Go and fill the bottle you already paid for. That is the whole trick.

options.es: In der Stadt? Das ist nicht sauber.
options.en: In town? That is not clean.
options.feedback: It comes off the mountain and it is colder and cleaner than the bottle in your hand.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Das macht jeder am Anfang. Ade.
steps.en: Everybody does that at the start. Goodbye.

options.feedback: She told you something useful and did not make you feel stupid. That deserves the full merci vielmal.
Correct, and it skips the thank you she had earned.

options.en: I am not at the start.
options.feedback: You are, and she was being kind about it.
